summary: This bash script connects to an Oracle database using sqlplus (Oracle's command-line tool) with system administrator credentials, then runs a series of SQL commands to set up a pluggable database and execute initialization scripts that create and populate an HR (Human Resources) schema.

explanations.3: The `<<EOF` syntax starts a here-document, which lets us pass multiple lines of input to sqlplus as if we typed them interactively. The `%%variable%%` placeholders are template markers that get replaced with actual values before this script runs.
explanations.4: This SQL command switches the database context to a specific pluggable database (a partition within Oracle) so subsequent commands run in that isolated environment.
explanations.6: The `@` symbol in sqlplus means 'execute this SQL script file', so this line runs the hr_create.sql script to set up the HR table structure.
explanations.7: Similar to line 6, this runs the hr_populate.sql script to fill the HR tables with sample data.
